key_insight: The paper reframes estimate generation in regularised reinforcement learning as a recommendation problem. Its central idea is to evaluate the quality of the resulting estimates, rather than sampling efficiency alone.
problem_solved: Bandit-based estimation frameworks typically assess how efficiently samples are collected, but do not directly measure the quality of the policy, value, or Q-value estimates used during training and inference.
method: Formalise estimate generation as a recommendation process.
Treat bandit-based sampling as an operator that improves recommendations.
Introduce a recommender-regret perspective for estimation with bandits and Monte Carlo tree search; the supplied abstract is truncated, so specific definitions and results are unavailable.
impact: This perspective could help practitioners evaluate whether additional sampling produces better estimates for regularised RL. It shifts attention toward estimator usefulness, though the provided excerpt does not establish empirical gains.
visual_elements: Pipeline: bandit sampling → improved recommendation → policy, value, or Q-value estimate.
Side-by-side comparison: sampling efficiency versus estimate quality.

paper_title: Recommender regret for improving regularised RL estimation with bandits and MCTS
paper_authors: Danilo Vucetic, Alexandre Larouche, Mohammad Pedramfar, Audrey Durand, Gauthier Gidel
